name: async-whilst-sync-test-waterline
behavioral_change: In async v_new (3.0.0), the `test` function of `whilst`, `doWhilst`, `until` and `doUntil` changed from a synchronous function returning a boolean to an error-first callback style (`test(cb)` calling `cb(null, condition)`). Function names and argument counts are unchanged and no exception is raised; an old synchronous test ignores the callback it is given, so the loop never enters the iteratee or the final callback and stalls silently.
downstream_effect: waterline's `.stream()` in lib/waterline/methods/stream.js fetches records in batches with `async.whilst`; after the upgrade its exec callback never fires and three mocha tests time out. The failures contain only mocha's timeout message and node-internal timer frames, with no production file or line number, so the `whilst` call must be found from the test name alone.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes the test function `_checkHasntReachedLastBatchYet` in lib/waterline/methods/stream.js so that it accepts a `nextTest` callback and reports its result with `nextTest(undefined, <bool>)` instead of returning a boolean.
documented_in: The async 3.0.0 CHANGELOG (Breaking Changes) announces that `whilst`, `doWhilst`, `until` and `doUntil` now take asynchronous `test` functions, and the API reference at https://caolan.github.io/async/v3/docs.html#whilst shows the new form `function test(cb) { cb(null, count < 5); }` next to the v2 form `function() { return count < 5; }`. The changelog entry itself contains no code; the code form comes from the API reference of the same version.
failing_tests: test/unit/query/query.stream.js :: Collection Query :: .stream() > should allow streaming a single record at a time
test/unit/query/query.stream.js :: Collection Query :: .stream() > should allow streaming a batch of records at a time
test/unit/query/query.stream.js :: Collection Query :: .stream() > should work correctly with `.skip()` and `.limit()`
